# LumaFlow H1 2026 Business Report

> **Fictional test fixture:** LumaFlow, its products, competitors, research, customers, and every figure in this report are invented solely to test the `interactive-html-presentation` Skill. Nothing here describes a real company or market.

**Reporting period:** January 1–June 30, 2026  
**Currency:** U.S. dollars  
**Prepared:** July 15, 2026

## Executive Summary

LumaFlow is a fictional workflow-automation software company serving mid-market and enterprise operations teams. During the first half of 2026, revenue reached **$6.6 million**, up **32%** from **$5.0 million** in H1 2025. The company ended June with **480 customers**, compared with 375 one year earlier, an increase of **28%**. Annual recurring revenue (ARR) was **$15.0 million** on June 30, 2026, up from $11.5 million on December 31, 2025.

Growth came primarily from the mid-market subscription business and improved conversion of qualified product trials. Gross customer retention was **91%**, while net revenue retention was **108%**. These measures are distinct: gross retention excludes expansion revenue, while net retention includes upgrades and contraction. Management’s priorities for H2 2026 are improving enterprise onboarding, reducing infrastructure costs, and delivering planned analytics capabilities.

## The Problem

Operations teams at companies with 200–5,000 employees often coordinate recurring work across email, spreadsheets, ticketing systems, and chat. In LumaFlow’s fictional 2026 survey of **240 operations leaders**, 64% said fragmented tools caused missed handoffs at least monthly, and 47% said they could not measure process completion consistently. The survey was conducted online in February 2026 among respondents in the United States and Canada; results reflect respondent opinion and are not independently audited.

Existing enterprise automation platforms can require long implementations, while lightweight task tools may lack permissions, audit trails, or cross-system controls. LumaFlow estimates that a typical target customer maintains 18 recurring processes across at least four tools. This estimate is based on 60 fictional customer interviews completed between October 2025 and March 2026.

## The Solution

LumaFlow provides a web-based workflow platform with reusable process templates, conditional approvals, audit logs, and integrations with common business systems. Customers can map a process, assign responsibility, set service-level reminders, and review completion data without writing code.

The product is positioned between basic task management and complex enterprise automation. Its primary promise is faster deployment with sufficient governance for operational teams. Median initial deployment time for customers launched in H1 2026 was **21 days**, measured from signed agreement to first live workflow. This is an actual fictional historical result, not a guarantee for future customers.

## Market Opportunity

LumaFlow’s fictional internal market study estimates the North American workflow-operations software market at **$2.4 billion in 2026**, growing to **$3.6 billion in 2030**. That change implies a calculated compound annual growth rate of approximately **10.7%** over four years. The estimate covers subscription software for recurring operational workflows at organizations with 200–5,000 employees; it excludes general project management and robotic process automation.

The company identifies a serviceable obtainable market of **$480 million** in 2026, equal to 20% of the estimated total market. This is a management estimate based on target industries, company size, geography, and current product capabilities. It should not be presented as audited market data or guaranteed revenue potential.

## Product Performance

H1 2026 revenue consisted of **$4.2 million** from mid-market subscriptions, **$1.8 million** from enterprise subscriptions, and **$0.6 million** from implementation services, totaling **$6.6 million**. The comparable H1 2025 figures were $3.0 million, $1.4 million, and $0.6 million, totaling $5.0 million. Segment growth was therefore 40% for mid-market subscriptions, approximately 28.6% for enterprise subscriptions, and 0% for services.

Qualified-trial conversion improved from **10% in H1 2025 to 14% in H1 2026**, an increase of 4 percentage points. Average monthly active users per customer increased from 38 to 46. Gross customer retention improved from 88% to 91%, and net revenue retention improved from 103% to 108%. All retention figures cover the trailing twelve months ended June 30 of the stated year.

## Competitive Comparison

The following fictional comparison reflects vendor materials and 30 buyer evaluations reviewed by LumaFlow in June 2026. It is directional and has not been independently verified.

| Vendor | Starting annual price | Median deployment | Gross retention | Integrations |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| LumaFlow | $15,000 | 21 days | 91% | 48 |
| NorthstarOps | $22,000 | 35 days | 89% | 60 |
| TaskHarbor | $12,000 | 45 days | 84% | 32 |

LumaFlow leads this comparison in deployment speed and gross retention, but NorthstarOps offers more integrations and TaskHarbor has the lowest starting price. Pricing excludes implementation services and may vary by contract size.

## Timeline

- **January 22, 2026 — Completed:** Released the conditional-rules engine.
- **March 31, 2026 — Completed:** Reached 450 customers.
- **May 18, 2026 — Completed:** Opened an EU-hosted data environment.
- **June 30, 2026 — Completed:** Reached 480 customers and $15.0 million ARR.
- **September 30, 2026 — Planned:** Release self-service process analytics.
- **December 31, 2026 — Target:** Reach $18.0 million ARR.

Planned milestones and targets are forward-looking management expectations, not achieved results.

## Risks and Constraints

The top 10 customers represented **24% of ARR** on June 30, 2026, creating concentration risk. Cloud infrastructure expense equaled **18% of H1 2026 revenue**, above management’s 15% target. Enterprise deployment capacity is constrained by a six-person implementation team, and the product plan assumes eight additional engineering hires by December 2026.

The market estimates rely on internal research, competitor information may be incomplete, and survey findings may not generalize beyond the sampled respondents. The $18.0 million year-end ARR target depends on planned product delivery, continued conversion improvement, and no material increase in customer churn.

## Conclusion

LumaFlow entered H2 2026 with higher revenue, more customers, improved conversion, and stronger retention than in the comparable prior periods. Its advantages are deployment speed and mid-market subscription growth. Its most important constraints are customer concentration, infrastructure cost, implementation capacity, and execution risk around planned hiring and analytics delivery. The evidence supports investment, but forward-looking targets must remain separate from historical results.
